title: LEGO 71053 Shrek Gingy 'cracks' might just be moulding marks
summary: Fans spotted apparent cracks on the new LEGO Gingy minifigure from 71053 Shrek, but an experienced injection-moulder says they could simply be witness lines from the manufacturing process.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Since LEGO 71053 Shrek minifigures went on sale, several fans have shared photos showing what look like cracks around the head of the new Gingy minifigure. The community largely assumed these were genuine defects, especially given recent reports of a separate crack found on some Patrick minifigures from the same set.

However, an AFOL with professional plastic injection-moulding experience — including designing LEGO-compatible custom minifigure parts — has offered an alternative explanation to Brick Fanatics. According to this fan, the marks are likely "witness lines," a normal by-product of the injection-moulding process where molten plastic flows together from two injection points, or around an internal pin, and cools slightly as it joins along a flat surface. This can leave a visible seam that looks crack-like but isn't necessarily a structural fault.

This explanation is not an official statement from the LEGO Group, and Brick Fanatics has said its team is examining its own Gingy minifigures more closely, alongside the confirmed genuine crack reported separately on some Patrick pieces.

**Rumour label:** The cause of the Gingy marks remains unconfirmed — this is community and expert speculation, not an official LEGO Group explanation.

## Why it matters
Quality concerns spread quickly in the LEGO fan community, and it's easy for normal manufacturing features to be mistaken for defects. If these marks are indeed witness lines rather than cracks, it's a useful reminder for collectors not to assume the worst before getting expert or official confirmation — useful knowledge for anyone building a Shrek-themed collection or checking minifigure quality before display.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for any official comment from the LEGO Group on the Gingy minifigure, plus further community testing to see whether the marks affect durability or are purely cosmetic.
